name: resizable

arguments.name: $direction
accepts: none, both, horizontal, vertical, block, inline or auto, in any case
a CSS-wide keyword, var(), or null to leave resize out; a quoted keyword is written without its quotes

arguments.name: $overflow
accepts: one or two of visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto and overlay, such as hidden auto
a CSS-wide keyword on its own, var(), or null to leave overflow out; a quoted value is written without its quotes

caveats: `resize` only applies to an element whose computed `overflow` is not `visible`, which is why `$overflow` defaults to `auto`. Passing `visible` back in is refused: measured in Chrome 152 by dragging the corner, a box with `overflow: auto` went from 204x84 to 274x130 and the same box with `overflow: visible` did not move and had no grabber drawn, and Firefox 156 draws the grabber on the first and not the second. A pair with one visible axis is not dead and is not refused: `visible hidden` computes to `auto / hidden` in Chrome and Safari 26.6.2 alike.

`null` still leaves `overflow` out, for a caller who sets it elsewhere. Nothing in the mixin can see that, so it is not refused, but `resize` will do nothing if the element's overflow is `visible` where it lands.
